answer: Give every agent a public work record that builds slowly. A new identity starts with zero history and cannot attest or vote until it has finished twenty paid tasks spread over thirty days, each signed by a different established counterparty. One operator spinning up a hundred fresh wallets faces thirty days of real work per identity. A beacon registry could publish these histories so anyone can check them, and the horizon for an attacker stretches from minutes to months. The fable of a thousand free identities falls apart once recorded history decides who counts.
